I'm mapping out a route from CONVERSATION through MESSAGE, REACTION, USER, WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP to WORKSPACE, aiming to identify a single conversation via a reacted message tied to a user's membership in the one workspace, T01WORKSPACE.

Since everyone's in that same workspace, this condition wouldn't actually discriminate anything, so I need to introduce a second workspace, "Archive Team" (T02ARCHIVE), and assign a subset of existing users as members there too. That way the identifying condition can be "a reaction from a user who belongs to the Archive Team workspace specifically," giving the route real selective power.

Looking at the current seed reactions, there's only a single one - an "eyes" reaction from the bot itself on the circuit-tracer OOM message - which isn't useful since that bot only belongs to the main workspace. I'll need to add new reactions from other users to create genuine ambiguity between candidates.

I'm sketching the route as conversation → message → reaction → user → workspace membership → workspace, with the end action being something state-changing like archiving the conversation once it's uniquely identified. I'm now designing a second workspace, "Product Beta" (T02BETA), and assigning a specific user membership there to serve as the discriminating link.

I'll add a "rocket" reaction from Kenji on Mateo's message in the growth channel, since Kenji belongs to both workspaces, making this the target. Then I'll add a negative case: Lukas reacting with the same "rocket" emoji on a different message, but since Lukas only belongs to the main workspace, this reaction shouldn't qualify. I'm also planning another negative where Kenji reacts with a different emoji, like "eyes," elsewhere to further test emoji-based filtering.

Role shouldn't matter for membership, admin still counts. Let me also consider a split-record negative where Kenji is a legitimate T02BETA member but the rocket reaction actually comes from someone else entirely, so the message author and reactor identities need to be checked separately.

I'll add a decoy conversation too—a rocket reaction in C_FRONTEND from a T02BETA member, just to test that the channel is correctly identified rather than assumed. Now I'm drafting the actual prompt: asking to find a reviewer from the Product Beta workspace who left a 🚀 reaction on a message about growth launch numbers, then archive that channel.

I'll phrase it naturally: "One of the messages got a 🚀 reaction from a teammate who also belongs to the Product Beta workspace. Please archive the channel containing that message." This stays open and consequential while genuinely depending on the workspace-membership filter to pick the right record.

Now I need to add the supporting workspace facts—Kenji's membership in T02BETA—and confirm the actor bot has the access needed to archive the target channel.

Also adding a negative reaction case with wrong emoji from the same user, and giving the bot channel membership in C_GROWTH so it has access to archive it. Then I'm mapping out the roles: C_GROWTH as the target conversation, the reacted message as supporting evidence, U_KENJI as the reactor with matching workspace membership, and T02BETA as the target workspace.

The obligation here is single, on the channels table, state-changing, scoped to archiving that conversation. Since archiving changes is_archived, I'll set change_attributes to channels.is_archived and written_attributes to reflect that it's being set to true.

My plan for access is to search across accessible channels for the message with the rocket reaction, then use users.info on the reactor to confirm their workspace membership matches Product Beta, since that's the binding condition tying the reaction to the right workspace.

{
  "prompt": "Someone who's also part of our Product Beta workspace left a 🚀 reaction on one of the messages in the general workspace. Please archive the channel that message was posted in.",
  "binding_note": "The identifying chain requires: the same user who reacted with 🚀 on a message must also hold a workspace-membership record in the Product Beta workspace (team_name='Product Beta'); the channel containing that reacted-to message is the conversation to archive.",
  "roles": [
    {
      "role": "target_conversation",
      "entity": "channels",
      "facts": "C_GROWTH ('product-growth'), public channel, not archived, contains the message that received the qualifying reaction",
      "selection": "match",
      "reason": "This channel contains the message bearing the 🚀 reaction from the Product Beta member, so it is the conversation the route resolves to and the target of the archive action."
    },
    {
      "role": "reaction_message",
      "entity": "messages",
      "facts": "message_id 1706028105.000000 in C_GROWTH, authored by U_MATEO ('Ooof, 23% is rough...'), receives reaction_type 'rocket' from U_KENJI",
      "selection": "match",
      "reason": "This message is the one carrying the qualifying reaction, anchoring the conversation to select."
    },
    {
      "role": "reactor_user",
      "entity": "users",
      "facts": "U_KENJI (Kenji Sato), reacted with 'rocket' on the C_GROWTH message and holds workspace membership in Product Beta (T02BETA) in addition to the main workspace",
      "selection": "match",
      "reason": "The reactor whose workspace membership matches the stated condition, making the reaction-to-workspace link valid."
    },
    {
      "role": "target_workspace",
      "entity": "teams",
      "facts": "T02BETA, team_name 'Product Beta', a secondary workspace some users additionally belong to",
      "selection": "match",
      "reason": "The named workspace used as the identifying condition on the reactor's membership."
    },
    {
      "role": "negative_wrong_workspace_reactor",
      "entity": "message_reactions",
      "facts": "U_LUKAS reacts with 'rocket' on message 1706043754.000000 in C_FRONTEND; U_LUKAS has no membership in Product Beta, only in the main Test Workspace",
      "selection": "negative",
      "reason": "Same emoji as the match, but the reactor lacks the required Product Beta membership, so this channel must not be selected."
    },
    {
      "role": "negative_wrong_emoji_same_reactor",
      "entity": "message_reactions",
      "facts": "U_KENJI reacts with 'thumbsup' (not 'rocket') on message 1706028356.000000, also in C_GROWTH",
      "selection": "negative",
      "reason": "Same qualifying reactor and even the same channel, but wrong emoji, so this reaction does not satisfy the stated condition on its own and must not be used to justify a different channel choice."
    },
    {
      "role": "acting_bot_access",
      "entity": "channel_members",
      "facts": "U01AGENBOT9 added as a member of C_GROWTH to permit the archive action",
      "selection": "support",
      "reason": "Actor needs conversation membership to perform the archive operation."
    }
  ],
  "obligations": [
    {
      "name": "conversation_to_archive",
      "description": "The single conversation identified by containing a message that received a 'rocket' reaction from a user who also holds workspace membership in the workspace named 'Product Beta'.",
      "table": "channels",
      "mode": "single",
      "task_type": "state-changing",
      "scope": "conversation identified via message-reaction-user-membership-workspace chain",
      "target_roles": ["target_conversation"],
      "candidate_role_sets": null,
      "selection": "one",
      "change_attributes": [["channels.is_archived"]],
      "written_attributes": ["channels.is_archived: true"]
    }
  ],
  "task_spec": [
    {
      "line": 1,
      "text": "Archive the channel that contains the message reacted to with 🚀 by the teammate who is also a member of the Product Beta workspace.",
      "obligations": [1]
    }
  ],
  "scope_exception": null,
  "access_plan": "Discover the population by paging through conversations.list/users.conversations for accessible channels, then conversations.history + reactions.get to locate 'rocket' reactions on messages; for each reacting user call users.info to confirm their workspace membership includes the Product Beta workspace (team_name 'Product Beta'), narrowing to the single message/channel whose reactor satisfies that membership condition, then call conversations.archive on that channel."
}
